title: Presence in two adult worm maps gave no clear response sign agreement prediction gain in 445 selected pairs
abstract: We tested whether a chemical connection found in two adult worm wiring maps helps predict repeated response sign agreement. We linked the Witvliet adult maps to the Randi wild-type stimulation atlas. The selected sample had 445 directed neuron pairs, 80 source identities, 103 target identities and 4018 response observations. We used the proportion of observation pairs with the same response sign. A model controlled mean chemical count, electrical count, reverse chemical count, response-list length and cell identity. Five folds held out source identities. Adding presence in both maps changed mean squared error from 0.0232771 to 0.0233064. The reduction was -0.0000293, with a conditional 95% crossed-cell bootstrap interval from -0.0001650 to 0.0000901. No planned sensitivity check gave a clear positive gain. A strong simulated support effect was recovered. Response-list lengths differed from the atlas count field in 277 selected pairs. A post hoc count-match check also gave no clear gain. The test does not show equal function or within-animal reliability. Two anatomy samples, pooled responses, uncertain observation selection and limited count overlap restrict the result. Code, response values, source hashes and independent checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Mean sample sign agreement and added prediction value of chemical presence in both adult maps. Intervals are conditional 95% crossed-cell bootstrap limits. They do not account for fitting or animal identity. The count-match test was added after the primary data audit.
